You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

G=load()
def analyze(n):
    i=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; o=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    h,w=len(i),len(i[0]); bg=i[0][0]
    objs={(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if i[r][c]!=bg}
    r0=min(r for r,c in objs); r1=max(r for r,c in objs); c0=min(c for r,c in objs); c1=max(c for r,c in objs)
    ch=[(r,c,i[r][c],o[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if o[r][c]==2 and i[r][c]==bg]
    return i,o,h,w,bg,r0,r1,c0,c1,ch
for n in [1,2,3]:
    i,o,h,w,bg,r0,r1,c0,c1,ch=analyze(n)
    print('demo',n,'bbox',(r0,r1,c0,c1),'h w',h,w)
    # frame coverage
    frm=frozenset((r,c) for r in range(r0,r1+1) for c in range(c0,c1+1) if (r in(r0,r1) or c in(c0,c1)) and i[r][c]==bg)
    ch_set=set(ch)
    print('  frame filled?',frm<=ch_set, 'missing frame:',sorted(frm-ch_set)[:5])
    # interior fills in ch
    int_ch=[x for x in ch if not ((x[0] in(r0,r1) or x[1] in(c0,c1)))]
    print('  interior changes:',int_ch[:8])

def f(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0]); bg=collections.Counter(x for r in g for x in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    objs=[(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if g[r][c]!=bg]
    r0=min(r for r,c in objs); r1=max(r for r,c in objs); c0=min(c for r,c in objs); c1=max(c for r,c in objs)
    out=[r[:] for r in g]
    # top/bottom rows: fill bg between two object cells horizontally
    for r in (r0,r1):
        oc=[c for c in range(c0,c1+1) if g[r][c]!=bg]
        for a,b in zip(oc,oc[1:]):
            for c in range(a+1,b): out[r][c]=2
    # left/right cols: fill bg between two object cells vertically
    for c in (c0,c1):
        or_=[r for r in range(r0,r1+1) if g[r][c]!=bg]
        for a,b in zip(or_,or_[1:]):
            for r in range(a+1,b): out[r][c]=2
    return out
